title: unread-alerts
prompt: A depot reportedly slowed. I propose weather or staff shortage. One unverified customer report says loading took longer. No other information was supplied; nobody checked public alerts.
context: Public development case, not holdout data. Use Mode G. Evidence mode: reasoning-only; all supplied observations are hypothetical exercise inputs. No browsing or tools. Audience: operations lead; horizon: next 48 hours.

title: covered-negative
prompt: A sensor either detected a pressure excursion, lost calibration, or a dashboard misdisplayed its reading. In this hypothetical exercise, a separately calibrated recorder continuously covered the same pipe and period, with a detection threshold below the alleged excursion. Its verified record shows no excursion and no gaps. Compare these explanations.
context: Public development case, not holdout data. Use Mode G. Evidence mode: reasoning-only; all supplied observations are hypothetical exercise inputs. No browsing or tools. Audience: operations lead; horizon: next 48 hours.

title: dependent-reports
prompt: I propose equipment failure or unusual demand for a depot queue. A customer posted a photo, three blogs copied that photo, and our digest summarised those blogs. There are no independent observations. Assess these reports.
context: Public development case, not holdout data. Use Mode G. Evidence mode: reasoning-only; all supplied observations are hypothetical exercise inputs. No browsing or tools. Audience: operations lead; horizon: next 48 hours.

title: unknown-queues
prompt: Dispatch delays affect only lane X. I propose paperwork review or a processing backlog. We do not know whether lanes share a queue or use separate queues. Customer complaints increased. Rank the explanations.

title: coexisting-causes
prompt: Dispatch delays rose. Paperwork-review flags appeared, and a carrier outage was reported in the same period. I propose paperwork review or a carrier outage. Neither report is independently verified. Determine the dominant initiating cause without assuming the causes cannot coexist.

title: partial-logs
prompt: A settlement delay may reflect review holds, an internal queue, or a downstream failure. A sample of ten records shows no holds; queue logs cover only one of three workers. There is no downstream telemetry. A manager says these empty logs prove a downstream failure. Assess that conclusion.

title: weak-detector
prompt: A vibration excursion or sensor fault may explain an alarm. A backup detector reported no excursion, but its threshold is higher than the alleged event. Compare the explanations.

title: mismatched-window
prompt: A depot slowed between 12:00 and 14:00. I propose an outage or excess demand. An equipment status check at 09:00 was normal; no data cover the slowdown period. Assess whether the check rules out an outage.

title: intervention-confounding
prompt: A queue fell after both staffing and routing rules changed simultaneously. I propose staff shortage or routing inefficiency as the original cause. A manager attributes the improvement solely to new staffing. Assess the rival explanations.

title: zero-disconfirmation
